summary: Confirmed DONE (PR #710, 60633eff3). The shutdown telemetry flush is now capped at 300 ms. Effect v4's timeoutOption resumes as soon as the sleep wins and does not wait for the losing fetch, and runMain calls process.exit after a signal, so the in-flight POST cannot hold the exit. An unbounded `analytics.flush` that the old provider finalizer also ran (f1be4abc7 ProviderService.ts:2402) is gone. All adapter stopAll paths run concurrently. Copilot stops are bounded at 1 s and then force-stopped; forceStop only signals and does not wait. opencode gets SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after 1 s. Shutdown phase markers are logged, the desktop SIGKILL grace is 3 s on every stop path, and the perf harness disables telemetry. Tests cover the analytics bound, the parallel provider stop and the Copilot force-stop. What is left is cosmetic or adjacent and optional.

evidence.note: The finalizer runs clearScheduledFlush, then flush, under Effect.timeoutOption(300 ms). On timeout it logs at debug level and drops the events.

timeoutOption = raceFirst(asSome(self), sleep). raceAllFirst forks interruptible daemon children and resumes on the first exit. Losers are only interrupted when the parent exits, so the timeout returns at 300 ms even inside an uninterruptible finalizer.
After SIGINT/SIGTERM, runMain calls process.exit(code) once the main fiber ends, so a detached runFlushNow fetch or the losing flush fiber cannot keep the process alive.
it.live 'bounds the shutdown flush when the telemetry host is slow' uses a host that sleeps 3 s and asserts that shutdown takes under 2000 ms. The auditor said this test did not exist.
adapter.stopAll() runs with concurrency 'unbounded'. Test: ProviderService.test.ts:470 'stops every provider in parallel during shutdown'.

The provider finalizer no longer flushes analytics. Old code at f1be4abc7 ProviderService.ts:2402 ran `yield* analytics.flush` with no bound, a second unbounded network wait that the finding did not list.

1 s budget, then forceStop. The SDK's forceStop (copilot-sdk client.js:847) only SIGKILLs and disposes, with no waitForChildExit. Callers: CopilotAdapter.session.ts:268, :613 (stopSessionRecord), :672 (stopAll unbounded), CopilotProvider.ts:157 and CopilotTextGeneration.ts:108/146/250. There is no raw client.stop() left in apps/server/src.
SIGTERM, then forceKillAfter 1 s. The patched spawner (NodeChildProcessSpawner.js:343-357) polls the process group and SIGKILLs. OpenCodeAdapter.ts:811-815 and :2919-2923 stop sessions concurrently.
HTTP graceful shutdown is capped at 750 ms. The patched NodeHttpServer.js:100-108 sends 1001 to WebSockets first. This is the paired 20 s WebSocket fix.

'shutdown phase' logInfo markers: started, http-drained, runtime-services-closed. Attribution is coarse but present, and the runStopAll and sendBatch Effect.fn spans also land in the local trace file.

DESKTOP_BACKEND_SIGTERM_GRACE_MS = 3000 and exit wait 5000. stopBackendAndWaitForExit (main.ts:3370-3386) is the only SIGKILL path, used for relaunch (main.ts:1466), update install (:2829) and before-quit (:4890). The old hard-coded 2_000 SIGKILL is gone.
The Agent Control loopback listener releases with closeAllConnections() before close(). The +20.36 s tail from the report cannot recur.

fixDefects: No functional defect. Three comments are stale and still say the desktop SIGKILLs after 2 s, while the grace is now 3 s: apps/server/src/telemetry/Layers/AnalyticsService.ts:21, apps/server/src/server.ts:201-202 and apps/server/src/provider/Layers/CopilotAdapter.clientStop.ts:5. A timed-out flush drops the batch that is in flight, because Ref.modify removes it before sendBatch, and Effect.catch does not catch interruption. That is the drop-on-timeout behaviour the proposal intended.
implementationSketch:
Required (trivial): update the three stale '2 s' comments to say 3 s, or refer to the desktop's DESKTOP_BACKEND_SIGTERM_GRACE_MS.

Optional adjacent follow-ups, none part of this finding, all low value:
(a) ProviderService.runStopAll (ProviderService.ts:2461 and 2485-2500) reads the whole provider_session_runtime table twice (listThreadIds and listBindings). It then runs one getByThreadId SELECT and one autocommit UPSERT per row on every shutdown, including rows that are already 'stopped'. The user's real DB has 750 rows (748 stopped). A raw node:sqlite benchmark of that loop is about 48 ms at synchronous=FULL for 750 rows and about 132 ms for 3000 rows, before Effect/Schema overhead, and it grows with thread history. Fix: add a repository method that marks every non-stopped row stopped and merges the runtime payload in one UPDATE inside one transaction (WHERE status != 'stopped'). Alternatively, filter the existing loop to bindings whose status is not 'stopped'. Reuse a single list() call. Add a ProviderService.test.ts case that asserts already-stopped bindings get no per-row upsert at shutdown.
(b) Attribution: inside runStopAll, wrap each adapter.stopAll() in Effect.timed and log the instance id and ms, so the runtime-services-closed stage can be split by provider.
(c) The Tailscale Serve teardown (server.ts:750-797, in serverApplicationLayer) closes before the provider stops and may take up to TAILSCALE_SERVE_TIMEOUT_MS = 10 s (packages/tailscale/src/tailscale.ts:7). That is beyond the 3 s desktop grace, so a hung tailscaled would get the backend SIGKILLed before provider children stop. Pass a shutdown-specific timeoutMs of about 1 s to disableTailscaleServe. This only matters when Tailscale Serve is enabled.
(d) apps/desktop/scripts/startup-timing-smoke.mjs:289-294 childEnv does not set RYCO_TELEMETRY_ENABLED=false, so local runs of the desktop perf smoke send PostHog events. Add it.
decisionReason: Comment and internal shutdown hygiene only. No auth, E2EE, hosted lifecycle or Hub protocol impact.
correction: The auditor said AnalyticsService.test.ts has no test for the 300 ms shutdown timeout. One exists: AnalyticsService.test.ts:264-307 ('bounds the shutdown flush when the telemetry host is slow', with a 3 s host and a < 2000 ms assertion), added in 60633eff3. The auditor also did not mention that the old provider finalizer ran its own unbounded analytics.flush (f1be4abc7 ProviderService.ts:2402). The fix removed it, which strengthens DONE. Their other evidence checks out.
